value:
The legend is said to have taken place in Krita Yugam. Parashara Maharishi was said to

have been performing tapas when three demons by the name Thanjakan, Dhandakan, and

Gajamukhan started to interrupt him. It is then that Parashara Maharishi asked Lord

Vishnu to intervene and help him. The Lord mounted Garudan and first released his

Sudarshana Chakram to deal with Thanjakan. On his deathbed, Thanjakan asked the Lord

to name the land where he died to be named after him. Thus the land where he died

became Tanjavur. Next, the Lord went after Dhandakan. The Lord took the form of Varaha

and bore his teeth into Dhandakan and dug through the land, emerging out of Srimushnam.

Dhandakan asked for the land where he was buried to be named after him. Thus emerged



the Dhandaka Vanam. The last demon Gajamukhan was killed by the Lord in his Narasimha

form. Thus the three temples were put together to form one kshethram known collectively

by the name of Tanjai Mamanikoyil.
note: Record-level: the source's legend explains why the 3 temples together form one kshethram; not attributable to a single shrine.
